item.title: Why the decline curve runs low: wells that bounce back
item.description: About 35 to 50% of wells recover after the training window. A low month just before the forecast multiplies the typical miss by two to five, but does not explain all of it.

item.title: Gas has a season. Oil mostly doesn't.
item.description: Alberta and BC gas run 6 to 10% above trend in winter and below it through summer and early autumn. Oil barely moves with the calendar.

item.title: Most licensed wells aren't producing
item.description: Alberta's well file lists about 668,000 wells and about 143,000 reported production in the last year. Saskatchewan: 158,000 and 42,000.

item.title: Shut-ins and restarts: how many wells stop, and do they come back?
item.description: Of the wells producing in January 2022, 84% in Alberta, 82% in Saskatchewan and 73% in BC were still producing in September 2026; about one well in ten had a gap of three months or more.

item.title: Are new wells getting better? First-six-month rates by year
item.description: Alberta gas wells that first produced in 2025 started 19% stronger than 2022 starters at the median; Saskatchewan oil wells were roughly unchanged.

item.title: How concentrated is production? Licensee shares in Alberta and Saskatchewan
item.description: The five largest licensees hold 52% of Alberta's producing wells and 70% of Saskatchewan's; Saskatchewan's largest alone holds 27% of oil volume.

item.title: Gas-oil ratios: an "oil well" is not the same everywhere
item.description: Alberta crude-oil wells have a median gas-oil ratio of about 1,896 scf/bbl, Saskatchewan about 693, and Alberta bitumen wells about 352.
